Strengths:
The course was extremely educational as a methodology class. Especially when compared with similar courses at other universities, the syllabus was exceptionally well-designed and comprehensive. It provided one of the strongest possible frameworks for understanding research methodology in architecture, and it was highly beneficial for my academic development.
Weaknesses:
The shift from one day to two days per week during the semester was somewhat challenging in terms of workload and scheduling. However, this change was ultimately reasonable, particularly considering the value of the guest lectures and the dedicated session for abstract discussions.
It was great that Bülent Hoca had great connections with different academics who provided good methodology studies which developed critical thinking on academic research.
the instructor was always inclusive, encouraging and respectful to the class
course: The course has well-organized content that builds concepts step by step and connects theory with practical examples.
It was nice experiencing different methodologies, but it could be better if there are variety of weekly assignments.

Strengths:
One of the strongest aspects of the course was the opportunity to closely engage with a wide range of research methodologies. The inclusion of reviews across different types of work (such as books and articles) was particularly valuable, as it exposed us to diverse approaches and analytical frameworks.
Weaknesses:
However, we were not always able to fully communicate or convey the content of our peers’ book and article reviews to one another. Similar to the way abstracts were discussed collectively on a weekly basis, it would have been beneficial to have more shared and structured discussions around these reviews.

The course requires students to get out of their comfort fields of study and explore. However, assignments become too repetitive and discourage and drain students as the semester ends. They require students to fit into the given structure rather than critical engagement.

for theory based course, the structure was really well designed. It was not boring at all, and practical with the weekly assignments. This course really contributes to our intellectual knowledge with in class discussions and the relevant amount of assignments

instructor: Starting the department by taking a studio course with Bülent Hoca and Banu Hoca has been incredibly productive for our cohort. Their communication with us, both inside and outside the studio, their belief in our profession and in us, and their efforts to spark our interest in the subject were remarkable. It feels like Bülent Hoca was born to be an academic, and he provided us with invaluable guidance and broadened our horizons in many ways.  The only downside I can mention is that he expected us to come to critiques with finished drawings and didn't provide much feedback by drawing himself. Perhaps he believed this approach would help us grow, but I'm not entirely sure.  He is well aware of Bilkent's reputation as a challenging school and the heavy workload of our department. He always took this into account in his conversations with us. I am truly grateful to him for this semester and for everything he has done.

The department studio is definitely going to be an intense experience—never underestimate it. You are expected to think like both an urban designer and a landscape architect, which means you need to work on improving yourself in every aspect.  Come prepared for this demanding pace, and no matter how challenging it gets, understand that grades are not the most important thing. Focus solely on your personal growth and development.

In the future, I would absolutely love to become an urban designer as accomplished as she is. Thank you so much for everything, Hocam, and a special thank you for making the studio feel like home for us.
